$comment: Schema compatibility of every migration (docs/decisions/managed-db.md MD-01…MD-12; apps/server/src/db/compat.ts). A migration's version is schemaBase + its journal position: this chain's baseline stands for the 76 migrations of the chain before it, so it is version 77 and versions never go down (docs/decisions/report-trackers.md). readers/writers: the oldest binary schema (a migration tag) that can still read/write the schema the migration produces. Classes: expand, backfill, contract, incompatible.

0000_baseline.note: The whole schema of a new Whombat in one migration, at version 77. A database of the chain before it is refused with the release that moves it across (db/compat.ts).

0001_web_search.note: Web search's two nullable columns on burrows (docs/decisions/web-search.md); the release before it reads and writes past them.

0002_tracker_fix_release.note: A followed fix's production release (docs/decisions/report-trackers.md): one nullable jsonb column on tracker_fixes; the release before it reads and writes past it.

0003_job_result.note: A job's result as a message (docs/decisions/t3code.md): a nullable jsonb column on messages and a nullable text column on t3_watches; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0004_repo_icons.note: A repository's own icon for the Chat list (docs/decisions/chat-inbox.md): a new table repo_icons and a partial index on automation_runs.thread_root_id; the release before it never reads them.

0005_prompt_merge.note: A prompt's “Merge into main when it’s done” (docs/decisions/prompts.md): a boolean column with a default on prompts and a nullable jsonb column on t3_watches; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0006_tracker_separate.note: What a tracker offers of the part it releases on its own, and whether a followed fix changes it (docs/decisions/report-trackers.md): a nullable jsonb column on tracker_cursors and a nullable text column on tracker_fixes; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0007_own_address.note: The own address (docs/decisions/own-address.md): three new tables (the box's certificates, foreign certificates, box passkey user handles), nullable columns on appliance_passkeys and appliance_state with one defaulted switch, and an existing box marked as started with the shared route; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0008_link.note: Whombat Link (docs/decisions/whombat-link.md): a phone's own push token and the handle control gave the box for it on appliance_endpoints, and the Link stop the owner was pushed about on appliance_state, all nullable; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0009_mail_triggers.note: Mail-arrives automation triggers (docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md): two new tables mail_cursors and mail_trigger_items; the release before it never reads or writes them. Mail runs themselves live in automation_runs, which that release does advance, and it would ask the agent for one as the person: so a mail run, and a run with a connection_actions step, is stored with deadline_at at the epoch, which that release checks before any step of a started run and fails it (AR-68). Since 0015_runtime_releases a box makes and runs mail automations only while the release it would go back to knows them (AR-73); the epoch deadline stays for a box that goes back further. Writer floors stay at the baseline: a rollback stays read-write.

0010_dutch_voice.note: Opt-in Dutch voice (docs/decisions/desk-display-talk.md): a defaulted boolean switch and three nullable agreement columns (who, when, licence version) on voice_typing; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0011_mail_trigger_sync.note: Mail trigger activation time on automations and Message-ID deduplication on mail_trigger_items: nullable columns and a partial unique index; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0012_mail_read_failures.note: Consecutive full-read failure counts per message id on mail_cursors so unreadable emails skip cleanly after 3 attempts: one nullable jsonb column; the release before it reads and writes past it.

0013_mail_trigger_attachments.note: Ready attachment ids handed over from matched incoming emails on mail_trigger_items: one defaulted text[] column; the release before it reads and writes past it.

0014_outsiders_run_mark.note: The outsiders' mark in a column of its own (docs/decisions/outsiders-turns.md): a defaulted boolean messages.outsiders_run, set on messages that a tracker or mail run posted in its thread (what its own steps posted there while it ran, and its own turns for nobody while they ran) and on any a newer build marked in provenance, whose provenance goes back to null; the search documents of marked messages and of approvals on their cards are deleted, and a tracker or mail run's document loses its error. provenance keeps only the two Feedback kinds, so the release before it sends every message to apps and backs it up as it always did, and reads and writes past the column.

0015_runtime_releases.note: The runtime releases that ran on this database (docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md): a new table runtime_releases, where each release from this one on records itself at its first start on a managed box. A box makes, turns on and runs automations started by mail, or that change things in connected services, only while the release it would go back to after a failed update (from the manager's update facts) is in it, so the release before this one never runs on a database that has them: on a box updated from that release they stay off, and the next release turns them on. The release before it never reads the table.

0016_link_mail.note: Email through Whombat Link (docs/decisions/link-email.md): two defaulted booleans on appliance_state, the owner's choices; the release before it reads and writes past them.

0017_findmy_places.note: Find My as a connection (docs/decisions/findmy-connection.md): a new table findmy_places, each person's last known place words and since when on a Find My connection a live automation listens to, cascading with the connection. It also marks the first release that runs findmy automations: a box turns them on only while the release it would go back to recorded at least this schema in runtime_releases. The release before it never reads the table.

0018_findmy_timeline.note: A Find My timeline (docs/decisions/findmy-timeline.md): two new tables, findmy_timeline_people (whose days a Find My connection keeps, by Find My's id and name, since when) and findmy_stops (one row per stretch where the reads of a kept person said the same: a place's words, street and the geocoder's spot, no location, or a background read that didn't work, with its first and last read), both cascading with the connection. Rows whose last read is over 30 days old are deleted by each background pass. The release before it never reads either table.

0019_findmy_watches.note: One-time Find My watches (docs/decisions/findmy-watch.md): a new table findmy_watches, each watch the assistant started (whose, leaves or arrives, the card's place words, where they were while it watches, its thread and card, its status), kept when the connection goes (its connection_id set null, so the watch can say it stopped), cascading with the conversation and the agent. The release before it never reads the table; a findmy_watch card it finds shows as its message's text.

0020_onepassword_sync.note: A 1Password vault kept in step with the Vault (docs/decisions/onepassword-sync.md): two new tables, vault_onepassword_links (one row per pair of a Vault entry and a 1Password item: its state, the item's version and time, the base as an HMAC per field, never a value; the entry set null when it is removed, so the item is archived next) and vault_onepassword_state (one row per 1Password connection: what the last pass saw and how it ended), both cascading with the connection. The release before it never reads either table, and offers no 1Password connection.

0021_onepassword_pair_fields.note: The 1Password sync's pairs remember more (docs/decisions/onepassword-sync.md): on vault_onepassword_links the id of the one-time password field a pair follows, the entry id a lost create's marker carries (kept when the entry is removed, so its item is archived), and the HMACs of a change 1Password kept refusing (never a value), all nullable; on vault_onepassword_state the passes in a row that couldn't finish (default 0). The release before it never reads either table.

0022_onepassword_pull_first.note: After a whole-box restore 1Password's values win until a complete pass (docs/decisions/onepassword-sync.md): one boolean on vault_onepassword_state (default false). The release before it never reads the table.

0023_overview_layout.note: How the Overview is arranged (docs/decisions/overview-arranged.md): one nullable jsonb column on burrows. The release before it never reads or writes it, and a row it wrote reads as before there.

0024_uptime_checks.note: The hub check id and when the hub last took new probe settings, in two nullable columns on catalog_connections.

0025_incidents.note: Incidents (docs/decisions/monitoring.md MON-06, MON-09): a new table incidents, one row per stretch a server, connection or device was down or had a bad dot, with its words, cause and the push to withdraw, cascading with the burrow and kept 90 days. The release before it never reads the table.

0026_quiet_windows.note: Keeping things quiet for a while, causes and the way out (docs/decisions/monitoring.md MON-04…MON-08): three new tables. The release before it never reads or writes them.

0027_incident_automation_watches.note: Automations started by something going down or coming back, and one-time watches (docs/decisions/monitoring.md MON-90…MON-99): two new tables, incident_triggers (one claim per automation and incident, with a delayed start's due time) and thing_watches (each watch the assistant started, its thread and card), cascading with the burrow, and one nullable column on automations (thing_active_at). The release before it never reads or writes the two tables and reads and writes automations past the column. It can't read a definition with a thing trigger, though, yet would advance a run one started: this schema marks the first release that runs them, and a box makes, turns on and runs them only while the release it would go back to recorded at least this schema in runtime_releases.

0028_account_uptime.note: A new table keeps uptime samples for connected accounts and the burrow's GitHub connection.

0029_quiet_maintenance_left.note: Maintenance windows still to give back to the hosts service after a quiet window got a new one (docs/decisions/monitoring.md): one new table, quiet_maintenance_left. The release before it never reads or writes it.
